newsitem.title: UK: T-note/Bund gap seen swelling more after Greenspan. [CORRECTED 17:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: T-note/Bund gap seen swelling more after Greenspan. [CORRECTED 17:56 GMT]

text.p: The U.S. Treasury 10-year spread over Bunds ballooned to over 100 basis points on Wednesday and was seen widening up to 20 basis points further, after Fed chairman Alan Greenspan spoke of inflation dangers in the U.S.
"The risk always was that he would emerge on the hawkish side and attempt to verbally tighten monetary policy," said European bond strategist at Natwest Markets in London, Huw Roberts.
(Corrects attribution from "Yamaichi European bond strategist Adam Chester.")
"The trouble with the spreads is that we're at such wide levels already, but they probably have got more to go in the widening stakes."

Roberts said he expected the T-note/Bund spread to widen up to around 120 basis points over the next three months. By 1530 GMT the spread was at 99 basis points, after briefly touching 103, only the second time it has topped 100 for over a year.
Greenspan spooked bond and equity markets after delivering an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy, while noting inflation risks and saying rising stock prices warranted caution.
"Even I must admit that our economic prospects in general are quite favourable," Greenspan said in his semiannual Humphrey Hawkins testimony to Congress.
